description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/backend.rs:47-54

```rust
fn create_object<O: SetObject + Send + Sync>(
    &self,
    caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
    account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
    create_id: &str,
    obj: O,
) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = Result<(jmap_types::Id, O), BackendSetError<Self::Error>>>
       + Send;
```

The rustdoc says `create_id` is \"the client-side creation id used in
the `/set` request\". It does not say what the backend should DO with
it. Possible interpretations:

1. **Idempotency key.** If the client retries the same `/set` call,
   the backend uses `create_id` to detect and de-duplicate.
2. **Audit trail.** The backend logs which client-side id mapped to
   which server-side id for debugging.
3. **Reference target for in-batch ResultReference.** RFC 8620 §5.3
   allows `#c1` references that resolve from a `/set create` result.
4. **Ignore it.** Both the in-tree MemoryBackend (`memory.rs:491`,
   `_create_id`) and MockBackend (`lib.rs:337`, `_create_id`) take
   exactly this position.

A defensive backend implementor reading the trait doc cannot tell
which interpretation is canonical. The two in-tree impls have voted
\"ignore it\" — so why is it in the signature? Either:

- Document the intended semantics (likely #2 or #3, given how
  RFC 8620 §5.3 \"#cid\" reference resolution works in
  `jmap-server`'s ResultReference resolver).
- Remove the parameter from the trait if backends never actually
  consume it. The handler can pass the create_id straight to its
  own response-building logic without needing the backend to see it.

What goes wrong for callers when this stays as-is: a downstream
SharingBackend implementor either does nothing (matching MemoryBackend
and missing the RFC 8620 §5.3 reference-resolution opportunity if that
WAS the intended semantics) or guesses one of the four interpretations
above and ships divergent behavior across implementations. Real
contract gap that the rustdoc must resolve.
notes: Expanded SharingBackend::create_object rustdoc with explicit semantics of the create_id parameter: passthrough only, OPTIONAL backend uses are (1) audit logging, (2) idempotent retry detection. Clarified that #cid ResultReference resolution operates on the /set response's created map inside the Dispatcher, not on the backend's input — backends have no need to participate in #cid resolution.
title: SharingBackend::create_object create_id parameter — semantics undocumented; all in-tree impls ignore it
